item.title: On-Site Compost Program: Tools + Biochar Burn — Thu Nov 12, 12:00 PM — SRJC Shone Farm
item.description:
\(Español abajo\)
Please join us for a composting workshop taught by Bobby Nicholson of Compost Depot with the Sonoma Ecology Center \(SEC\) and SEC’s Sonoma Biochar Initiative \(SBI\). The workshop is funded by Zero Waste Sonoma \(ZWS\) and free to the public.
Let’s get our hands dirty! The workshop will provide practical guidelines and accessible soil science to build a healthy composting program on location with available resources and using a scalable model. Raymond Baltar of Sonoma Biochar Initiative will introduce the basics and science of biochar, including use of the flame cap kiln, and discuss the benefits of integrating biochar into a compost program. This will be a hands-on learning opportunity for farmers, agricultural producers, garden/greenhouse managers, and landscapers of all sizes. At the end of the workshop, attendees will have the resources and know-how to build a composting program on-site. Bobby is bilingual and can teach or answer questions in English and Spa

item.description:
Healthcare Forum 2026 & Resource Fair
Tickets Are On Sale Now!
Last November, almost 300 people showed up for "What's Changing in Healthcare and What To Do Next," our Healthcare Forum & Resource Fair. The atmosphere was unbelievable.
Regional experts, healthcare providers, and community leaders came together to cut through the noise and connect Sonoma County families with real healthcare resources.

item.title: Paint & Sip with Genevieve Elkin — Fri Nov 13, 5:30 PM — Petaluma Arts Center
item.description:
Join us for a relaxed and social paint & sip evening. You'll be guided step-by-step through painting a scenic view using acrylics, with plenty of room to make it your own.
Whether you follow along or add your own creative twist, the focus is on enjoying the process and having fun. Sip on a beverage, come with friends or meet new ones, and settle into a laid-back night of painting and connection. No experience needed - just show up and create.
Genevieve Elkin was Born and raised in Mill Valley, California and is a multidisciplinary artist now based in Petaluma. She earned a BFA in Illustration from Parsons School of Design and has professionally managed art departments, supporting artists and new media on high-profile projects. Genevieve loves painting, drawing, and exploring ceramics, and enjoys helping students experiment, have fun, and develop their own creative voice.
To learn more:@gennaelkin
Sponsored by
Source: Creative Sonoma, North Bay Bohemian

item.title: Come From Away: Marin's First Production of the Tony-Winning Musical — Fri Nov 13, 7:00 PM — Carol Franc Buck Hall of the Arts
item.description:
A Tony-winning Broadway hit is coming to San Anselmo, and it's the first time it's ever been performed in Marin.
**Come From Away**
Book, Music and Lyrics by Irene Sankoff and David Hein
On 9/11, 38 planes were suddenly grounded in a tiny town in Newfoundland. Overnight, the locals took in nearly 7,000 stranded travelers from around the world, and strangers became family. This is their true story, and it's funny, uplifting and full of heart, with a live band of musicians from Marin's Irish music scene.
San Domenico School's production marks the 25th anniversary of 9/11.
Show times:
**Friday, November 13 at 7pm**
**Saturday, November 14 at 1pm and 7pm**
**Sunday, November 15 at 3pm**
Tickets: $15 general, $10 students and seniors
Run time: About 2 hours, including intermission
Free parking. Wheelchair accessible.
**Saturday night still has the best seats!**

item.title: Summit Saturday at Calabazas Creek Open Space Preserve! — Sat Nov 14, 9:00 AM — Calabazas Creek Open Space Preserve
item.description:
Are you up for an adventure?
If you’re drawn to dramatic landscapes and hidden corners of Sonoma Valley, this hike is for you.
Join Sonoma Ecology Center for a FREE guided, moderately strenuous exploration of Calabazas Creek Open Space Preserve, a 1,290-acre protected gem nestled in the Mayacamas Mountains and shaped by both time and fire. This special outing, in partnership with Sonoma County Regional Parks and the Sonoma County Agricultural Preservation and Open Space District, offers a rare chance to traverse a preserve still closed to regular public access.
Starting from a forested trailhead near the heart of the 2017 Nuns Fire footprint, this route leads you through open meadows, dense oak woodlands, and along year-round streams—punctuated by seasonal waterfalls and stunning ridge-top vistas. item.title: Write & Collage: Words, Images & Memory — Sat Nov 14, 10:00 AM — Petaluma Arts Center
item.description:
Join Marlene Cullen for a creative two-hour experience that brings writing and collage together. In the first hour, guided freewriting prompts invite you to explore memorable moments, stories, and experiences in a welcoming, supportive environment. In the second hour, transform those reflections into a visual expression using images, colors, and textures.
No writing or art experience is necessary—just bring your curiosity and a willingness to explore.
Bring: A notebook and pen. Collage materials will be provided, and you're welcome to bring a favorite poem, magazines, photographs, or other materials you'd like to incorporate.
Marlene Cullen is the founder of Writers Forum and creator of Jumpstart Writing Workshops. Through her website and blog, The Write Spot, she shares resources and inspiration to help writers discover and develop their voices.
The Write Spot anthologies edited by Marlene are collections of short stories, poems, and vignettes with prompts to encourage writing.

item.title: Come From Away: Marin's First Production of the Tony-Winning Musical — Sun Nov 15, 3:00 PM — Carol Franc Buck Hall of the Arts
item.description:
A Tony-winning Broadway hit is coming to San Anselmo, and it's the first time it's ever been performed in Marin.
**Come From Away**
Book, Music and Lyrics by Irene Sankoff and David Hein
On 9/11, 38 planes were suddenly grounded in a tiny town in Newfoundland. Overnight, the locals took in nearly 7,000 stranded travelers from around the world, and strangers became family. This is their true story, and it's funny, uplifting and full of heart, with a live band of musicians from Marin's Irish music scene.
San Domenico School's production marks the 25th anniversary of 9/11.
Show times:
**Friday, November 13 at 7pm**
**Saturday, November 14 at 1pm and 7pm**
**Sunday, November 15 at 3pm**
Tickets: $15 general, $10 students and seniors
Run time: About 2 hours, including intermission
Free parking. Wheelchair accessible.
